chapter_theme: Bone and skull (எலும்பும் கபாலமும்): Siva rises bearing bones and a skull, and it is his bearing them that keeps the gods' bones and skulls from crumbling into earth.

371.reading: The strong one, first of the jewel-crowned gods, rose bearing bones and a skull; had he not borne them, those bones and skulls would have broken and become earth.
371.nuance: Tradition reads the bones and skulls as those of Brahma, Vishnu and the gods, which Siva wears after their deaths at the end of an aeon; by bearing them he keeps them. The verse says only that without his bearing them they would fall to dust. வலம்பன் is taken as 'the strong one'; it may be a corrupt or rare word.

links.note: Both turn to skulls. The Naladiyar's skulls in the burning ground grin at the living as proof of what the body comes to; Tirumular's are borne by Siva, and his bearing them is what keeps them from becoming dust. One image teaches the body's end, the other the Lord's hold even over what is dead.

source_issues: 371: வலம்பன் is unusual and its sense uncertain.
